Daily Devotional

November 16

35 I have shewed you all things, how that so labouring ye ought to support the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive. (Acts 20:35 KJV)

This statement by Jesus is not recorded in scripture that we have now, but Paul has attributed it to Jesus, and Jesus must have said it, or the early Church would have disputed it. It is certainly in line with all that Jesus taught, and is a powerful truth. There are two basic kinds of people on earth, givers and takers. Ones that are only takers are only concerned about themselves, and will take all they can get from you or society, as they are part of the “me generation”, that is all about what they want. The givers in life are the ones that have the peace of God manifest in their lives, and they joy in giving to others, and doing for others. Whether it is giving of your time, money, or possessions, they joy in being able to give to others, and are planting seeds for their future (2 Corinthians 9:9-10). Know that God gives to the givers of the world, as He wants to bless those that will be a blessing to others (Genesis 22:17).

All Christians should strive to help the weak and those in need, by being a giver of their time and money. The scriptures teach in many places, that we are supposed to always put others before ourselves, and help our neighbor when in need. If we all would do that, and let our light shine in this dark world (Matthew 5:16), then we would be glorifying our Lord, and showing that Christians represent a God who is love (1 John 4:8). In the natural we tend to be a taker, rather than a giver. If you will die to yourself, and let Christ live through you then you will be a giver, as Christ gave it all for us. You will enjoy the love and peace of God, when you become a giver, as that is fulfilling the commands of Jesus – to love your neighbor as yourself (Matthew 22:39). Be a giver and glorify God in all you say and do. Praise God for His goodness!

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com

Discovery is also available in criminal cases.[8] Under the rule set forth in Brady v. Maryland, the prosecutor is obligated to provide to the defendant any information that is exculpatory or potentially exculpatory, without any request by the defense. Further discovery is available if initiated by the defendant. For example, a discovery demand might be for production of the names of witnesses, witness statements, information about evidence, a request for opportunity to inspect tangible evidence, and for any reports prepared by expert witnesses who will testify at trial.[9]

If a defendant in a criminal case requests discovery from the prosecution, the prosecutor may request reciprocal discovery.[10] The prosecutor's right to discovery is deemed reciprocal as it arises from the defendant's request for discovery.
